title: 2006 HMMT February Guts Problem 6
statement: Suppose \(A B C\) is a triangle such that \(A B=13, B C=15\), and \(C A=14\). Say \(D\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{B C}, E\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{A D}, F\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{B E}\), and \(G\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{D F}\). Compute the area of triangle \(E F G\).

solutions.text: By Heron's formula, \([A B C]=\sqrt{21(21-15)(21-14)(21-13)}=84\). Now, unwinding the midpoint conditions yields \([E F G]=\frac{[D E F]}{2}=\frac{[B D E]}{4}=\frac{[A B D]}{8}=\) \(\frac{[A B C]}{16}=\frac{84}{16}=\frac{21}{4}\).
